title: WPMS/792/2010 of KRISHNA SEWA ASHRAM SOCIETY Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND and OTHERS

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND, AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition No.792 of 2010 (M/B)
Sri Krishna Sewa Ashram Society
C-2, Dhalwala Rishikesh
Dsitrict Dehradun
Through its President Dr. C. L. Kohli ... Petitioner
Versus
State of Uttarakhand and others .... Respondents
Dated:- 29th April, 2011
Hon'ble Tarun Agarwala, J.
 Heard Mr. Subhash Upadhayay, the learned counsel for the
petitioner, Mr. J. P. Joshi, the learned counsel for the H.N.B.
Garhwal University, Srinagar and Mr. Shailendra Nauriyal, the
learned counsel for the Uttarakhand Technical University.
2. The petitioner is a society registered under the Societies of
Registration Act and has its own hospital known as Sri Krishna
Hospital, which has all the infrastructure and facilities. In the
year 2006, the petitioner moved an application for affiliation
with H.N.B. Garhwal University, Srinagar. On this application,
the University conducted an inspection on 14th June, 2006. The
inspection committee recommended a temporary affiliation for
the academic session 2006-2007 permitting 30 seats in B.P.T.
(Bachelor of Physiotherapy) and 30 seats in B.M.L.T. (Bachelor
of Medical Laboratories Technology). The University, on the
basis of recommendation given in the inspection report, referred
the matter to the Chancellor for grant of temporary affiliation
where the matter remained pending and, eventually, the State
Government passed an order dated 25th February, 2010 granting
'no objection certificate' for affiliation to the University and
allowing the petitioner's society to fill 15 seats each in the course
of B.P.T. and B.M.L.T.
3. On the aforesaid basis, the petitioner admitted its students
and also approached the University to grant temporary affiliation

2
and conduct the examination. In the meanwhile, the University
was declared as a Central University w.e.f. 15th January, 2009 by
Act No.25 of 2009. Accordingly, the University by a letter dated
29.03.2010 intimated the petitioner that since the University has
been declared a Central University, it was no longer possible to
grant affiliation to the petitioner in view of the provision of
Section 4(f) of the Central University Act, 2009 which prohibited
the University to make any new affiliation.
4. Since the petitioner was stranded at the crossing and had
already admitted its students and there was no examination body
to conduct the examination, the petitioner approached the writ
court by filing the present writ petition seeking appropriate
directions.
5. The learned counsel for the petitioner pointed out to a
letter dated 15th April, 2010 written by the Secretary to the
Government addressed to the Vice Chancellor of the University
brining on record the discussion held between them agreeing
that since "no objection certificate" was granted belatedly, the
examination of the students admitted by the petitioner for the
session 2009-2010 would be conducted by the University and,
for the subsequent session, the examination would be conducted
by the Uttrakhand Technical University respondent no.3. Inspite
of this arrangement being made between the University and the
State Government, the University did not conduct the
examination.
6. This court by an interim order dated 08th June, 2010
directed the H.N.B. Garhwal University to conduct the
examination for the academic year 2009-2010, which was subject
to the final decision of the writ petition. Based on the interim
direction, the examination has been conducted by the University,
but, the results have not been declared. In para 10 of the writ
petition, the petitioner has categorically brought on record the

3
order of the State Government dated 15th April, 2010 wherein the
arrangement was made for holding the examination for the
University for the academic session 2009-2010. The H.N.B.
Garhwal University in para 8 of its counter affidavit admits to the
discussion that took place between the University and the State
Government and the issuance of the letter of 15th April, 2010 but
submitted that since the University became a Central University
it was not possible to grant new affiliation or to hold the
examination of the students admitted by the petitioner.
7. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties, this court
is of the opinion that since the process for affiliation had started
as far back as in the year 2006, the petitioner is not at fault, the
University is also not at fault since they had made the inspection
at the earliest opportune moment and had also recommended for
a temporary affiliation. The matter remained pending with the
State Government and, eventually, a "no objection certificate"
was issued by the State Government on 25th February, 2010, but
at that time, the H.N.B. Garhwal University became a Central
University and was governed by the Central Universities Act,
2009. Faced with this situation coupled with the fact that the
students were admitted whose career should not be jeopardized,
the State Government held discussions with the H.N.B. Garhwal
University and came out with a via-media, namely, the
examination would be conducted by the University which is a
examining body for the session 2009-2010 and affiliation and
examination would thereafter be done by the Uttarakhand
Technical University. The learned counsel for the Uttarakhand
Technical University admits the aforesaid arrangement made by
the State Government. The order of the State Government dated
15th April, 2010 has not been questioned either by the H.N.B.
Garhwal University or by the Uttarakhand Technical University.

4
8. In the light of the aforesaid and taking into consideration
the interest of the students, this court disposes of the writ
petition directing the H.N.B. Garhwal University to declare the
results of the examination which it had conducted for the session
2009-2010. The students, who are successful, will be admitted in
the Uttarakhand Technical University for the session 2010-2011
and it would be open to the Uttarakhand Technical University to
take necessary arrangements for inspection etc. with regard to
the affiliation of the petitioner's society at the earliest.
 (Tarun Agarwala, J.)
Dated 29.04.2011
Rawat
